instantiated_cells.justification: Lobbying as a lobbyist is prohibited unless licensed, and a 'lobbyist' is a paid individual whose duties include lobbying (with a 5-days-per-reporting-period threshold when duties are mixed), so paid lobbyists must obtain a license to lobby.
A lobbyist license (the operative credential for lobbyists) expires on December 31 of each even-numbered year, implying renewal/filing on a biennial (24-month) cycle.
Lobbyists must file a license application, while principals must separately file a registration statement upon exceeding the $500 threshold, indicating separate filings by each party.
The lobbyist license application must include items like a social security number and signature, but no photograph requirement is stated.
Elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees are not subject to specified lobbying regulation provisions when acting in an official capacity.
An agency that files a statement under §13.695 and named officials are exempt from multiple core lobbying requirements (licensing, registration, reporting, etc.) except as provided in §13.695.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled sections do not specify any lobbyist obligation to notify the commission of changes to a lobbyist’s license application/registration information (only agency statements under §13.695(2) have a 10-day change notice).

The statute requires a lobbyist to be licensed before lobbying (§13.66) but does not state a numeric deadline in days after first lobbying for the lobbyist’s own registration/licensure (it is a precondition rather than a day-count).
